summary: AWS deploy prep: moves the static-files + catch-all index.html handler after the /api routers (previously every GET to /api/* such as /api/user/email/activate/:token was swallowed and returned index.html), adds a public GET /api/user/status health check returning {message:'Ok'}, and gitignores ECS task JSON files.

statements.text: Nothing flagged (plain reads logins, payments, database changes and secrets. It doesn't run the code, and it can miss bugs.)
statements.why: Health route is public but returns only {message:'Ok'}; no login/payment/db/secret problem.

statements.text: + New server code that answers requests and works without logging in. /api/user/status
statements.why: routes/user.js wires GET /status with no checkAuth; handler returns {message:'Ok'}. The old 'lists data' wording is gone.

misses.what: Before this commit the catch-all app.get('*') sat before the API routers, so every GET API request (e.g. the email activation link /api/user/email/activate/:token) returned the React index.html instead of working; the app.js reorder fixes that. The card doesn't mention app.js.
